{{Use dmy dates|date=January 2025}}

'''Hans Schneider''' (24 January 1927 – 28 October 2014) was a British-American mathematician, and James Joseph Sylvester Emeritus Professor at the [[University of Wisconsin–Madison]]. He was the first president of the International Matrix Group (1987–1990) and its successor, the [[International Linear Algebra Society]] (1990 – 1996), which established the triennial [[Hans Schneider Prize in Linear Algebra|Hans Schneider Prize]] in 1993.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.math.wisc.edu/hans-schneider|title=Memorial for Hans Schneider {{!}} Department of Mathematics|website=math.wisc.edu|language=en|access-date=2018-11-08|archive-date=1 October 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151001094107/https://www.math.wisc.edu/hans-schneider|url-status=dead}}</ref> Schneider was a founding editor (1968–1972) and then editor-in-chief of ''[[Linear Algebra and Its Applications]]'' (1972 – 2012)<ref>{{cite web|title=Linear Algebra and its Applications – Editorial Board|url=http://www.journals.elsevier.com/linear-algebra-and-its-applications/editorial-board/|publisher=Elsevier|accessdate=27 February 2013}}</ref> and an Advisory Editor of the ''[[Electronic Journal of Linear Algebra]]''.<ref>{{cite web|title=Electronic Journal of Linear Algebra|url=https://www.math.technion.ac.il/iic/ela/Home.html|accessdate=27 February 2013}}</ref><ref name="cv">{{cite web|last=Schneider|first=Hans|title=CV|url=https://people.math.wisc.edu/hans/vitae2014|accessdate=2024-07-21}}</ref>

He received his Ph.D. from the [[University of Edinburgh]] in 1952; his advisor was [[Alexander Craig Aitken]]. Following his doctorate, he taught at the [[Queen's University of Belfast]] until 1959, when he moved to the University of Wisconsin. He retired in 1993.<ref name="cv"/> He was the author of over 160 research papers. His research covered many topics in linear algebra, such as Perron Frobenius theory and related topics, inertia theory. and lately [[Max-plus algebra|max algebra]]. For his experiences in the years 1938 – 1940 see
the Kindertransport site.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.kindertransport.org/voices/schneider_personalHistory.htm | title=Voices of the Kinder: March 1938 – August 1940: A Personal History of My Family During 30 Turbulent Months | first=Hans | last=Schneider | date=March 2006 | publisher=The Kindertransport Association | accessdate=24 October 2018 }}</ref>

Schneider died of cancer at the age of 87.<ref name=hesselberg>{{citation |last=Hesselberg |first=George |title=Hans Schneider, a mathematician of the most linear kind, dies at 87 | newspaper=[[Wisconsin State Journal]] |date=28 October 2014 |url=http://host.madison.com/wsj/news/local/hans-schneider-a-mathematician-of-the-most-linear-kind-dies/article_5b231718-612f-536a-b102-d05cc748189b.html}}</ref>
He was the grandfather of [[YouTube]] musician / producer [[Kurt Hugo Schneider]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Hans Schneider, leading mathematician, dies|url=http://news.wisc.edu/23252|publisher=UW-Madison|accessdate=30 October 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=An old photo of my grandpa...|url=https://instagram.com/p/u9dfHDNyW6/|publisher=Kurt Hugo Schneider|accessdate=6 November 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Lilies for Hans 1/24/1927 -- 10/28/2014|url=https://instagram.com/p/vMC4-OA7E5/|publisher=Laurie S. Auth|accessdate=14 November 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=My parents, Hans and Miriam, at the airport in Madison|url=https://instagram.com/p/go1lZrDfUr/|publisher=Michael Schneider|accessdate=15 November 2013}}</ref>
